Results.Title: Enabled members inactive for more than 90 days
Results.SkipReason: Entra ID P1 licence (AAD_PREMIUM) not detected.
Results.Description: Lists enabled member accounts whose last successful sign-in is older than **90** days, including accounts that never signed in and were created before the threshold.
Results.Rationale: Unused accounts accumulate access, licences and group memberships that nobody reviews.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Review the listed accounts with their managers.
2. Disable accounts that are no longer needed.
3. Remove licences and group memberships after the retention period.

Results.Title: Enabled licensed users inactive for more than 90 days
Results.SkipReason: Entra ID P1 licence (AAD_PREMIUM) not detected.
Results.Description: Same as ARG.ENT.001, restricted to users with at least one licence assigned.
Results.Rationale: Licences assigned to inactive users are a direct cost with no business value.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Confirm the users are no longer active.
2. Remove the licences or reassign them.

Results.Title: Guests inactive for more than 90 days
Results.SkipReason: Entra ID P1 licence (AAD_PREMIUM) not detected.
Results.Description: Guests that accepted their invitation but have not signed in for **90** days.
Results.Rationale: Stale guest accounts keep access to Teams, sites and files long after the collaboration ended.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Run an access review for guests.
2. Remove guests that are no longer needed.

Results.Title: Guests that never accepted the invitation (more than 30 days)
Results.Summary: 14 of 212 guests have not accepted their invitation for 30+ days.
Results.Description: Guests with `externalUserState` = PendingAcceptance whose invitation is older than **30** days.
Results.Rationale: Unredeemed invitations clutter the directory and can be redeemed later by whoever controls the mailbox.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Confirm whether the collaboration is still needed.
2. Delete the pending guest or resend the invitation.
Remediation.PowerShell:
# Sample only - review before running
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.ReadWrite.All'
Remove-MgUser -UserId '<ObjectId>'

Results.Title: Disabled users that still have licences
Results.Summary: 6 of 87 disabled users still have licences assigned (shared, room and equipment mailboxes excluded).
Results.Description: Disabled accounts with licences, excluding shared, room and equipment mailboxes (detected through Exchange Online).
Results.Rationale: Licences on disabled accounts are paid for but unusable.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Check whether the mailbox must be retained (convert to shared or apply a hold).
2. Remove the licences.

Results.Title: Global Administrator count outside 2 to 4
Results.Summary: 6 Global Administrators found (active assignments); the recommended range is 2 to 4. Eligible PIM assignments not evaluated: Entra ID P2 not detected.
Results.Description: Counts active (and, with Entra ID P2, eligible) assignments of the Global Administrator role, expanding role-assignable groups.
Results.Rationale: Too few Global Administrators is a recovery risk; too many widens the blast radius of a compromised account.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Keep two emergency-access accounts.
2. Move day-to-day administration to least-privileged roles.
3. Remove unnecessary Global Administrator assignments.

References.Title: Best practices for Microsoft Entra roles

Results.Title: Privileged roles assigned to guests
Results.Summary: No directory role is assigned to a guest (143 assignments evaluated).
Results.Description: Any directory role assignment whose principal is a guest user.
Results.Rationale: Administrative access should be held by accounts the organisation controls.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Remove the role assignment from the guest and assign it to an internal account.

References.Title: Best practices for Microsoft Entra roles

Results.Title: Security groups without owners
Results.Summary: 22 of 318 security groups have no owner.
Results.Description: Assigned (non-dynamic), non-role-assignable security groups with zero owners.
Results.Rationale: Without an owner, nobody is accountable for membership reviews.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Identify the business owner of each group and add them as owner.

References.Title: Manage who can create Microsoft 365 groups

Results.Title: Stale devices (no sign-in for more than 180 days)
Results.Summary: 3,000 of 8,412 devices have not signed in for 180+ days.
Results.Description: Devices whose `approximateLastSignInDateTime` is older than **180** days.
Results.Rationale: Stale devices make device-based reporting unreliable and clutter the directory.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Disable stale devices.
2. After a grace period, delete them.
3. Make sure BitLocker recovery keys you still need are preserved.
Remediation.PowerShell:
# Sample only - review before running
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'Device.ReadWrite.All'
Update-MgDevice -DeviceId '<Id>' -AccountEnabled:$false

Results.Title: Guest invitations are restricted
Results.Summary: Guest invitations are allowed for admins, guest inviters and all members (allowInvitesFrom = adminsGuestInvitersAndAllMembers).
Results.Description: Reads `authorizationPolicy.allowInvitesFrom`.
Results.Rationale: Letting every member invite guests is acceptable in some organisations but should be a deliberate decision.

Remediation.Steps: 1. In **External collaboration settings**, restrict guest invitations to admins and users in the Guest Inviter role if appropriate.

Results.Title: Users can register applications
Results.Summary: All users can register applications (defaultUserRolePermissions.allowedToCreateApps = true).
Results.Description: Reads `authorizationPolicy.defaultUserRolePermissions.allowedToCreateApps`.
Results.Rationale: Uncontrolled app registrations make application ownership and credential hygiene hard to govern.

Remediation.Steps:
1. In **User settings**, set *Users can register applications* to **No**.
2. Assign the Application Developer role to users who need it.

References.Title: Add credentials to an app registration

Results.Title: Users can create tenants
Results.Summary: Non-admin users cannot create tenants.
Results.Description: Reads `authorizationPolicy.defaultUserRolePermissions.allowedToCreateTenants`.
Results.Rationale: Tenants created by users fall outside central governance.

Remediation.Steps: 1. In **User settings**, set *Restrict non-admin users from creating tenants* to **Yes**.

Results.Title: Directory synchronisation freshness
Results.SkipReason: Cloud-only tenant: directory synchronisation is not enabled.
Results.Description: Fails when `organization.onPremisesLastSyncDateTime` is older than **24** hours.
Results.Rationale: A stalled sync leaves leavers enabled in the cloud.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Check the health of Microsoft Entra Connect / Cloud Sync.

Results.Title: Client secrets expiring within 30 days
Results.Summary: 4 client secrets on 4 of 162 app registrations expire within 30 days.
Results.Description: Password credentials whose `endDateTime` falls within the next **30** days.
Results.Rationale: Expired secrets break integrations; planned rotation avoids outages.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Create a new secret.
2. Update the consuming service.
3. Delete the old secret.

References.Title: Add credentials to an app registration

Results.Title: Expired client secrets still present
Results.Summary: 9 expired client secrets are still present on 7 app registrations.
Results.Description: Password credentials whose `endDateTime` is in the past.
Results.Rationale: Expired credentials are clutter and hide which credentials are really in use.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Delete expired secrets from the app registration.

References.Title: Add credentials to an app registration

Results.Title: Certificates expiring within 30 days
Results.Summary: No certificate expires within 30 days (41 certificates evaluated).
Results.Description: Key credentials (usage Verify) whose `endDateTime` falls within **30** days.
Results.Rationale: Expired certificates break app-only integrations.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Upload a new certificate, update the service, then remove the old one.

References.Title: Add credentials to an app registration

Results.Title: Expired certificates still present
Results.ErrorMessage: Response status code does not indicate success: 429 (Too Many Requests). Retry limit (5) reached for GET /v1.0/applications.
Results.Description: Key credentials whose `endDateTime` is in the past.
Results.Rationale: Expired certificates are clutter.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Remove expired certificates from the app registration.

References.Title: Add credentials to an app registration

Results.Title: App registrations without owners
Results.Summary: 17 of 162 app registrations have no owner.
Results.Description: App registrations with zero owners (owners fetched with JSON batching).
Results.Rationale: Ownerless apps have nobody responsible for credentials, permissions and lifecycle.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Assign at least one owner (ideally two) to each app registration.

References.Title: Add credentials to an app registration

Results.Title: Client secrets with a lifetime above 24 months
Results.Summary: 5 client secrets have a lifetime longer than 24 months.
Results.Description: Password credentials whose lifetime (`endDateTime` minus `startDateTime`) exceeds **24** months.
Results.Rationale: Long-lived secrets are rarely rotated and outlive the people who created them.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Replace the secret with one of shorter lifetime, or move to a certificate or managed identity.

References.Title: Add credentials to an app registration

Results.Title: Unused licences per SKU
Results.Summary: 3 of 9 paid SKUs have more than 10% or more than 5 seats unused.
Results.Description: Compares `prepaidUnits.enabled` with `consumedUnits` for each paid SKU; free and viral SKUs listed in the configuration are ignored.
Results.Rationale: Unused seats are recurring cost.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Reduce the subscription quantity at the next renewal, or reassign the seats.

Results.Title: Licence assignment errors
Results.Summary: No licence assignment errors (1,391 users evaluated).
Results.Description: Users whose `licenseAssignmentStates` contain an entry in state Error.
Results.Rationale: Assignment errors leave users without the services they are expected to have.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Resolve the conflict (for example missing usage location or conflicting service plans) and reprocess.

Results.Title: Shared mailboxes with a licence
Results.Summary: 2 shared mailboxes have a licence; this is required only above 50 GB, with an archive or with a hold.
Results.Description: Shared mailboxes (Exchange Online) whose user object has licences assigned.
Results.Rationale: Shared mailboxes do not need a licence unless they exceed 50 GB, have an archive or are on hold.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Check size, archive and holds.
2. Remove the licence where it is not required.

Results.Title: Public Microsoft 365 groups
Results.Summary: 11 of 486 Microsoft 365 groups are public (8 are Teams).
Results.Description: Microsoft 365 (Unified) groups with `visibility` = Public; the TeamEnabled column shows whether a team is connected.
Results.Rationale: Anyone in the organisation can join a public group and read its content.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Review each public group with its owners.
2. Switch groups that hold restricted content to Private.
Remediation.PowerShell:
# Sample only - review before running
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'Group.ReadWrite.All'
Update-MgGroup -GroupId '<GroupId>' -Visibility 'Private'

References.Title: Manage who can create Microsoft 365 groups

Results.Title: Microsoft 365 groups and Teams without owners
Results.Summary: 4 of 486 Microsoft 365 groups have no owner (3 are Teams).
Results.Description: Microsoft 365 groups with zero owners.
Results.Rationale: Ownerless groups cannot renew under an expiration policy and nobody manages membership or guests.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Assign at least two owners per group.

Results.Title: Microsoft 365 groups and Teams with a single owner
Results.Summary: 38 of 486 Microsoft 365 groups have exactly one owner.
Results.Description: Microsoft 365 groups with exactly one owner.
Results.Rationale: A single owner is a single point of failure when that person leaves.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Add a second owner to each group.

Results.Title: Group expiration policy configured
Results.Summary: No Microsoft 365 group expiration policy is configured.
Results.Description: Reads `groupLifecyclePolicies`; an empty list fails.
Results.Rationale: Without expiration, unused groups and Teams accumulate indefinitely.

Remediation.Steps:
1. In Entra admin center > Groups > Expiration, set a lifetime (for example 365 days).
2. Apply it to all or selected groups.

Results.Title: Microsoft 365 group creation is restricted
Results.Summary: All users can create Microsoft 365 groups and Teams (EnableGroupCreation = true).
Results.Description: Reads the Group.Unified directory setting `EnableGroupCreation`.
Results.Rationale: Unrestricted creation suits some organisations; others prefer a request process.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Decide on a creation policy.
2. If needed, restrict creation to a security group.

References.Title: Manage who can create Microsoft 365 groups

Results.Title: Group naming policy configured
Results.Summary: A naming policy is configured (prefix "GRP-").
Results.Description: Reads `PrefixSuffixNamingRequirement` and custom blocked words in the Group.Unified setting.
Results.Rationale: Consistent names make groups easier to find and govern.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Configure a prefix/suffix naming policy.

Results.Title: Inactive Teams (more than 180 days)
Results.Summary: Usage reports return concealed names (admin/reportSettings.displayConcealedNames = true), so inactive objects cannot be identified. Turn the setting off to evaluate this check.
Results.Description: Teams whose last activity in the D180 Teams activity report is older than **180** days.
Results.Rationale: Inactive Teams hold content nobody curates.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Archive or delete inactive Teams after confirming with their owners.

Results.Title: Teams with guests and no owner
Results.Summary: No ownerless team has guest members.
Results.Description: Intersection of ownerless Microsoft 365 groups that are Teams and groups with guest members.
Results.Rationale: Guests in an ownerless team are not reviewed by anyone.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Assign owners and review guest membership.

Results.Title: Orphaned sites
Results.Summary: 3 group-connected sites belong to a group without owners. Classic and communication sites were not evaluated (PnP.PowerShell not connected).
Results.Description: Group-connected sites whose group has zero owners (Graph). Classic and communication sites without valid site administrators are evaluated through PnP.PowerShell when connected.
Results.Rationale: Orphaned sites have nobody to manage permissions, sharing and retention.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Assign owners to the connected group, or site administrators to the site.

References.Title: Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive

Results.Title: Inactive sites (more than 180 days)
Results.Summary: Usage reports return concealed names (admin/reportSettings.displayConcealedNames = true), so inactive objects cannot be identified. Turn the setting off to evaluate this check.
Results.Description: Sites whose last activity in the D180 SharePoint site usage report is older than **180** days.
Results.Rationale: Inactive sites keep content and permissions nobody reviews.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Confirm with owners, then archive or delete inactive sites.

Results.Title: Tenant external sharing level
Results.Summary: Sharing allows Anyone links (sharingCapability = externalUserAndGuestSharing).
Results.Description: Reads `admin/sharepoint/settings.sharingCapability`.
Results.Rationale: Anyone links can be forwarded without authentication; some organisations accept this for specific scenarios.

Remediation.Steps:
1. Decide whether Anyone links are needed.
2. If not, set the tenant level to *New and existing guests*.

References.Title: Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive

Results.Title: Sites near their storage quota (more than 90%)
Results.Summary: No site uses more than 90% of its storage quota (402 sites evaluated).
Results.Description: Sites where storage used / storage allocated in the site usage report exceeds **90**%.
Results.Rationale: Sites that hit their quota become read-only for uploads.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Increase the quota or clean up content.

Results.Title: OneDrive of deleted or disabled users with content
Results.Description: OneDrive accounts (usage report) whose owner is deleted or disabled and that still hold content.
Results.Rationale: Leaver OneDrives hold business data that should be transferred or retained deliberately.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Transfer needed content to a manager, then let retention apply.

Results.Title: Shared mailboxes with sign-in enabled
Results.Summary: 3 of 41 shared mailboxes have sign-in enabled on the user object.
Results.Description: Shared mailboxes whose corresponding user account has `accountEnabled` = true.
Results.Rationale: Shared mailboxes should be accessed through delegation, not by signing in to them directly.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Block sign-in for the shared mailbox user account.
Remediation.PowerShell:
# Sample only - review before running
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.ReadWrite.All'
Update-MgUser -UserId '<ObjectId>' -AccountEnabled:$false

Results.Title: Distribution groups without owner
Results.Summary: 7 of 96 distribution groups have no owner (ManagedBy empty).
Results.Description: Distribution groups whose `ManagedBy` is empty.
Results.Rationale: Without an owner nobody approves membership changes.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Set at least one owner on each distribution group.

Results.Title: Inactive user mailboxes (more than 90 days)
Results.Description: User mailboxes whose last activity in the mailbox usage report is older than **90** days.
Results.Rationale: Inactive mailboxes may belong to leavers.

Remediation.Steps: 1. Confirm with the manager, then convert or remove the mailbox.
